title: Kernel telemetry adoption roadmap and operational playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a pragmatic adoption roadmap for kernel-level telemetry across the serving runtime. It ties runtime architecture intent, kernel scheduling observability, profiling playbooks, benchmarking signals, runbook integration, and release gating into a single operational plan intended for the runtime, SRE, and observability teams.

Scope: collection, normalization, storage, alerting, dashboards, rollout gating, and runbook integration for kernel signals (dispatch latency, kernel execution time, occupancy, memory amplification, KV cache hit-rate traces and causal chain IDs). Excludes agent diagnostics below host OS and third-party accelerator firmware traces (these are handled by HW partners).

Intended audience: runtime-engineers, scheduler-owners, observability, SRE, incident response leads, and release managers.

High-level goals

- Produce a stable, cost-bounded telemetry surface for kernel scheduling decisions and post-incident forensics.
- Ensure telemetry can be sampled or downsampled without compromising root-cause signal fidelity for SLO slices.
- Provide a release gating checklist so kernel or scheduler changes are not shipped without traceability.

Key signals and instruments

The telemetry surface will be organized into three tiers (Tier 0 = mandatory, Tier 1 = recommended, Tier 2 = experimental). Each signal has a collection frequency and retention recommendation.

| Signal | Tier | Frequency | Retention (hot) | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| dispatch.enqueue-latency_ms | Tier 0 | 1s aggregation | 30d | runtime-coordinator | Per-tenant percentiles (P50/90/99) and raw sample on error cases |
| kernel.exec-duration_ms | Tier 0 | per-request sample + 5s agg | 30d | kernel-dispatcher | tag by kernel-variant and model-variant |
| kernel.occupancy_pct | Tier 1 | 10s | 14d | scheduler-agent | GPU occupancy by slice, include concurrent kernels |
| kvcache.lookup-latency_ms | Tier 0 | 1s sample | 60d | kv-cache | correlate with session IDs and prefix-hash |
| kernel.memory-watermark_mb | Tier 1 | 30s | 14d | allocator | record soft-oom triggers, per-node |
| trace.causal-id | Tier 0 | sampled per-request | 90d | runtime-trace-proxy | GUID propagated across services for causal stitching |
| kernel.quantize-fallback-count | Tier 2 | event-driven | 7d | model-onboarding | experimental: measure automatic quantization fallbacks |

Collection and normalization rules

1. Use the runtime-trace-proxy to stamp a trace.causal-id at the API ingress. Persist causal-id in the request header (X-Redwood-Causal-ID).
2. Kernel and scheduler components MUST emit events with causal-id and the minimal context: tenant_id, model_id, kernel_variant.
3. Numeric timings must be in milliseconds with integer precision. Counters in integers. Percentages reported as integers 0-100.
4. Normalization pipeline (observability ingestion) will:
   - deduplicate by (causal-id, kernel-uuid, timestamp)
   - normalize field names according to the signal ontology above
   - enrich with topology tags: node_id, numa_zone, accelerator_type
5. Keep raw compressed traces for error windows and on-call requests (see retention overrides below).

Storage and cost guardrails

- Hot retention targets: Tier 0 signals 30d hot, Tier 1 signals 14d hot. Hot = queryable at sub-5s latency.
- Cold archive: daily compressed bundles moved to object storage (S3/GCS) after hot window. Cold retention policy: 365d for causal-linked incidents, 180d for default.
- Budget constraints: telemetry 3E3D 5% of per-month runtime spend requires approval by SRE lead. Telemetry ingest rates must be simulated in the benchmark suite before expanding collection.

Signal sampling and fidelity strategy

- Baseline: for normal operation, sample 10% of low-latency /low-cost requests for full trace payload; always collect Tier 0 aggregated counters (percentiles).
- On spikes, autoswitch to triggered sampling: when scheduler P99 latency > SLO threshold (P99 > target * 1.25), increase full-trace sampling to 100% for affected tenants for 10 minutes.
- For releases flagged in the canary matrix, run shadow full-trace collection at 100% for canary cohorts only.

Gating and release checklist (pre-merge and pre-release)

Pre-merge (developer):
1. Add telemetry emitters for any new kernel_variant or scheduler path.
2. Unit tests that assert telemetry fields are set.
3. Update signal ontology doc and add a sample synthetic trace to the benchmark corpus.

Canary matrix (release manager):
1. Canary cohort running new kernel: 5% of traffic for 6 hours.
2. Telemetry checks during canary:
   - dispatch.enqueue-latency P99 increase < 10% vs baseline
   - kernel.exec-duration median change < 5%
   - error-rate on causal-id-tagged traces < 1% absolute increase
3. If any check fails, rollout must halt and revert or go to corrective patch.

Operational runbook integration

- When alerts fire for "kernel.exec-duration.p99 > threshold":
  1. Page oncall runtime-owner and scheduler-owner.
  2. Run quick triage using the "trace quick-attach" CLI to fetch representative traces for the last 15 minutes:
     - rtr-cli trace fetch --causal-window 15m --signal kernel.exec-duration_ms --format jsonl
  3. If traces show a new kernel-variant correlation, escalate to kernel-owner and open a triage-wide Jira.
  4. If no kernel-variant correlation, run the profiler sampling playbook (see "Profiling playbooks" section).

Profiling playbooks (summary)

- Microprobe sampling: use microprobe to capture kernel-level timings on a single node for synthetic replay. Steps:
  1. Isolate node (scheduler drain) and reproduce with the benchmark harness (bench-harness run --signature <signature>).
  2. Run microprobe with sampling rate 100Hz for 60s and export to /tmp/microprobe.tar.gz.
  3. Upload to the profiling bucket and attach to the incident.
- Continuous lightweight profiling: 1Hz kernel.exec-duration histogram applied to 1% of nodes, used for regression detection.

Benchmarking suite integration

- Before enabling new Tier 0 signals at production scale, run the "telemetry-ingest-sim" scenario in the benchmarking suite to estimate cost and query latency impact. Required check: simulated ingestion < 2x current ingestion and query latencies not > 1.5x.
- Bench commands example:
  - benchctl telemetry simulate --corpus telemetry-ingest-corpus-2026 --scale 10x
  - benchctl run --scenario telemetry-ingest-sim --assert ingest-multiplier<=2 --assert query-slo<=1.5

Dashboards and alerts (summary)

- Dashboards to create:
  - "Kernel Health" (team dashboard): P50/P90/P99 kernel.exec-duration, dispatch.enqueue-latency, kernel.occupancy_pct heatmaps by model family.
  - "Causal Forensics" (oncall): top traces attached to causal-id with quick links to KV cache lookup latency.
  - "Telemetry Cost" (infra): ingest rate, compressed size, projected monthly storage.

Alerting thresholds (suggested)

- dispatch.enqueue-latency.p99 > baseline.p99 * 1.25 for 5m -> P1 alert to runtime-oncall.
- kernel.exec-duration.p99 increase > 15% vs 24h baseline AND error-rate increase > 0.5% -> P0 emergency page.
- telemetry-ingest-rate > budgeted-ingest * 1.5 -> P2 alert; auto-scale ingestion buffer (see infra runbook).

Rollout phases and timeline

Phase A (Quarter 1, pilot, 6 weeks)
- Implement trace.causal-id stamping and ingest for 3 Tier 0 signals.
- Pilot on two non-critical tenants and run telemetry-ingest-sim to validate cost.
- Deliver: kernel health dashboard (alpha), profiling playbook template updated.

Phase B (Quarter 2, expansion, 8 weeks)
- Expand Tier 0 to all runtime nodes; enable sampling policy for Tier 1 signals.
- Integrate with benchmarking suite and release gating.
- Deliver: canary matrix rules enforced by release-orchestrator.

Phase C (Quarter 3, optimization, 6 weeks)
- Implement adaptive sampling and autoswitch logic in runtime-coordinator.
- Add queryable cold archive index for causal-linked incidents.
- Deliver: Telemetry cost dashboard and automated retention compressor.

Phase D (Quarter 4, refinement, ongoing)
- Add Tier 2 experimental signals and feedback into model-onboarding and quantization test harness.
- Run a cross-team retrospective and update SLOs as needed.

Owner and governance

- Runtime telemetry steward: Maya Patel (runtime observability).
- Scheduler instrumentation owner: Evan Rodriguez.
- SRE custodian for retention and cost: Lena Zhou.
- Review cadence: monthly telemetry governance meeting; quarterly cross-team review that ties to release windows.

Appendices

A. Example trace schema (JSON snippet)

{
  "causal_id": "cid-0a12b3c",
  "tenant_id": "t-42",
  "model_id": "gpt-rl-13b",
  "kernel_variant": "kern-v2a",
  "events": [
    {"name": "dispatch.enqueue", "ts_ms": 1700000000000, "value_ms": 2},
    {"name": "kernel.exec", "ts_ms": 1700000000020, "value_ms": 24}
  ]
}

B. Quick CLI snippets

- Stamp causal id locally for testing: export X_REDWOOD_CAUSAL_ID=$(uuidgen)
- Generate a synthetic trace: rtr-cli trace synth --signature small-chat --causal-id $X_REDWOOD_CAUSAL_ID --output trace.json
- Fetch attached traces for an incident: rtr-cli trace fetch --incident INC-1234 --format jsonl > incident_traces.jsonl

C. Retention overrides policy

- Incidents: any incident with severity P0/P1 will auto-promote its related causal traces to 365d cold-retention.
- Customer compliance: for Private deployment customers who require longer retention, open a retention-exception request; SRE custodian will evaluate costs and alternatives (on-prem archive or shorter ingest windows).

D. Open work items (initial backlog)

- Implement deduplication logic in ingestion pipeline (P0).
- Add causal-id propagation to SDK wrappers (P1).
- Add telemetry-ingest-sim scenario to benchmark suite with 10x load profiles (P1).
- Define exact field names and units in the signal ontology (P0).

If you own any of the open items above or have feedback, add comments to this page and @mention the owners listed in the governance section.
